sources.source_ref: RA 386 (1950), Civil Code of the Philippines — Quasi-Delict Provisions
sources.document_title: Republic Act No. 386 — Civil Code of the Philippines
verified_sections: Article 2176 — Quasi-delict defined: act or omission causing damage through fault or negligence
Article 2180 — Employer/principal liability for employees' negligent acts
Article 2189 — Owner/employer liability for employees'/contractors' negligent acts
Article 2194 — Solidary liability for quasi-delict when multiple parties cause damage
Articles 2191-2193 — Rules on apportionment of liability
sources.notes: Articles 2176-2194 establish the quasi-delict (culpa aquiliana) framework. Article 2176 is the foundational negligence provision; Article 2180 establishes vicarious liability of architects for employees.

sources.source_ref: RA 386 (1950), Civil Code of the Philippines — Prescription Periods
sources.document_title: Republic Act No. 386 — Civil Code of the Philippines
verified_sections: Article 1146 — Quasi-delict actions prescribe in 4 years from accrual of cause of action
Article 1144 — Written contract actions prescribe in 10 years
sources.notes: Article 1146 establishes the 4-year prescription period for quasi-delict claims, distinct from the 10-year prescription for written contracts (Article 1144) and the 15-year/10-year framework under Article 1723.

sources.document_title: Republic Act No. 9266 — The Architecture Act of 2004
verified_sections: Section 20(a) — AoR civil liability for plans, specifications, and contract documents
Section 20(b) — AiCC civil liability for construction supervision
sources.notes: Section 20 complements Civil Code quasi-delict provisions by establishing the architect's professional liability framework.
